R001.text: H001 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I consists of exactly n integers. We prove the string identities simultaneously by natural induction on t≥0. At t=0, hv=λv and xv=0 are H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v and, when t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v (with xv=0 at t=0). The relation hy=yh−2y from H002 gives h y^(t+1)v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. The relation xy=yx+h gives x y^(t+1)v=y(x y^t v)+h y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+λ−2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v, also at t=0 using xv=0. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction gives both identities for all t in their stated ranges.

For each i∈I, repeated application of the x identity in F001 gives x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. At i=0 the product is empty and equals 1; at i≥1 its factors are positive integers, since i≤λ. Since v≠0 by H003, this shows e_i≠0 over ℂ. F001 gives h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. To prove independence, fix coefficients c and temporarily assume L2: Σ_(i∈I)c_i e_i=0. Fix j∈I and apply ∏_(k∈I,k≠j)(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). Every term except j is zero; the j term is c_j [∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)]e_j. All its factors are nonzero complex numbers and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary, all coefficients vanish. Discharging L2 proves independence.

Apply M001 to the division ring ℂ, the complex vector space V, the finite index set I and the family e. F002 supplies independence, F001 gives |I|=n, and H002 gives dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n and finite dimensionality. Thus the span of e is V, so together with independence it is a basis. By F001, y^(λ+1)v has eigenvalue −λ−2 under h. Expand this vector in the basis e; comparison of each coefficient in h y^(λ+1)v=(−λ−2)y^(λ+1)v gives [λ−2i−(−λ−2)] times that coefficient zero. For i∈I this multiplier is 2(λ+1−i)≠0 in ℂ. Every coefficient is zero, hence y^(λ+1)v=0. Applying further powers of y gives all higher vanishing.

For arbitrary i∈I divide the identities F001 by i!: x e_0=0, and for i≥1, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1). Directly y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while y e_λ=0 by F003. Also h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. These are the required integer action matrices.

Fix r≥0. Iterating the x matrix in F004 and dividing by r! gives X(r)e_i=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_(i−r)=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i. When r>i, iteration reaches x e_0=0 and gives zero. Similarly iteration of y gives Y(r)e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ, and gives zero past the terminating string. These binomial coefficients have nonnegative top at least r. They are integers: for every nonnegative integer a₀, the factorial expressions have boundary values binom(a₀,0)=binom(a₀,a₀)=1 and satisfy binom(a₀,s)=binom(a₀−1,s−1)+binom(a₀−1,s) for 0<s<a₀ by a common-denominator calculation. Induction on a₀, proving the assertion simultaneously for all 0≤s≤a₀, proves integrality. This establishes every divided-power formula in the exported conclusion as well as its zero cases.

R002.text: Since p is prime by H001, p≥2 and the integers not divisible by p are multiplicatively closed. Fraction addition and multiplication therefore make R a subring of ℚ⊂ℂ; in particular every integer b with p∤b is a unit, with inverse 1/b∈R. By H004 choose a simultaneous integer basis B of M and complex basis B of V. It has finitely many vectors since V has finite dimension n by H002. M010 applied to the nontrivial commutative ring ℂ supplies its strong rank condition. M003 applied to its complex basis gives that its number of vectors is dim_ℂ V=n. By N001, |I|=n; reindexing the basis by I yields the existence stated in F001.

Choose m as in F001. Apply M002 with R₀=ℤ, A=M, S₀=R and the integer basis m. It gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_(i∈I) of M_R. The map ι_M sends these basis vectors to m_i; a finite R-linear relation among their images is also a complex-linear relation, so all coefficients are zero. Thus ι_M is injective, identifies M_R with the R-span of the m_i inside V, and its complex span is V. For any r≥0, admissibility H004 and D005 imply X(r)M⊂M and Y(r)M⊂M; R-linearity gives preservation of M_R. In particular X(1)=x and Y(1)=y preserve M; H002 gives h=xy−yx on V, so h preserves M as well. The commutators in H002 show directly that the integer span of x,y,h is bracket-closed, since all three structure constants are integers. For arbitrary t₀∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh and z_M∈M the restriction t₀z_M is in M. The rule (t₀⊗c₀)(z_M⊗d₀)=t₀z_M⊗(c₀d₀), for arbitrary c₀,d₀∈K, respects addition and both integer balancing relations, hence defines a K-bilinear action on the two tensor products. Its Lie representation identity is verified on pure tensors by the identity in the given complex Lie module V, and then on finite sums by bilinearity. Thus it is the asserted induced Lie action, without identifying the Chevalley integer form with any different reduction.

For every integer 0≤r≤λ, apply M006 with ℓ=p and u=r. H001 supplies primality and r≤λ<p, so p∤r!. Thus r! is a unit of R. In particular λ!, j!, (λ−j)! are all units, for j∈I. Their ratio binom(λ,j)=λ!/[j!(λ−j)!] is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ−j)!/λ!. The factorials are positive and therefore nonzero as rational numbers. These statements also cover r=0.

We now identify operators by their actions on the complex basis e from N001. In Y(λ)X(λ), every basis vector below e_λ is killed by X(λ); on e_λ, X(λ)e_λ=e_0 and Y(λ)e_0=e_λ. Hence Π=E_λλ. Next X(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, with coefficient binom(λ−λ+λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ. For ΠY(λ−j), an input e_k with k<j is carried below e_λ and killed by Π; if k>j the lowering string terminates and gives zero; on e_j its coefficient is binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j) and its image is e_λ. Therefore ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. All statements include λ=0, when every factor is the identity on the one-dimensional space.

Combining F004, or applying it to each e_k, gives X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_ij. Invert the coefficient using F003 to get E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F002 and R-linearity, hence every E_ij preserves M_R. With F002 and F003 this proves the entire exported conclusion.

R003.text: Use the embedding from N002 throughout to regard M_R as a submodule of V. By N001 its vectors have unique coordinates in e. Since E_ii preserves M_R by N002, the ith coordinate projection maps M_R onto J_i e_i. For arbitrary i,j₁∈I and c₁∈J_(j₁), E(i,j₁)(c₁ e_(j₁))=c₁ e_i∈M_R, giving J_(j₁)⊂J_i; the reverse inclusion follows by exchanging the two coordinate indices. Thus all J_i equal J. Choose the R-basis m of M_R supplied by N002. The finitely many ith coordinates of m generate J_i, since each vector of M_R is a finite R-linear combination of m, and conversely these coordinates lie in J_i by E_ii-stability. Hence J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: temporarily assume L1: J={0}. Then every coordinate projection of M_R would vanish, so M_R would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and the nonzero basis vector e_0 in N001. This contradiction discharges L1 and proves J≠{0}. Finally the maps M_R→J^I taking coordinates, and (c_i)↦Σ c_i e_i, are mutually inverse R-linear maps. The latter sum is in M_R since each c_i e_i is; independence in N001 gives uniqueness. This proves the direct sum decomposition without any rank assumption on a submodule of ℂ.

Define U and μ as declared, and choose a nonempty finite list g of nonzero R-generators of J from F001; let k≥1 be its length, and write it g_1,...,g_k. For any rational q₀ and any finite R-linear combination Σ_(j=1)^k r_j g_j, tensor bilinearity gives q₀⊗Σ r_j g_j=Σ(q₀r_j)(1⊗g_j). Consequently the finite set {1⊗g_j:1≤j≤k} spans U over ℚ. Apply M008 with F=ℚ and A=U to this finite set; since the span is all of U, U is finite-dimensional. To check injectivity of μ, let s₀≥0 be arbitrary, take arbitrary families Q_1,...,Q_(s₀)∈ℚ and C_1,...,C_(s₀)∈J, and set z₀=Σ_(l=1)^(s₀)Q_l⊗C_l. Every element of the algebraic tensor product has such a finite-sum presentation. Define D to be the product of the positive denominators of the Q_l (the empty product is 1), and put H_l=D Q_l∈ℤ. Then D is a nonzero integer and tensor balancing over R, which contains ℤ, gives z₀=(1/D)⊗Σ H_l C_l. Temporarily assume L2: μ(z₀)=0. Its image is (1/D)Σ H_l C_l, so Σ H_l C_l=0 in ℂ, hence z₀=0 in U. Discharge L2. Since the finite presentation was arbitrary, the kernel of μ is zero, which proves injectivity by applying this to the difference of any two tensors with equal images. Its image is exactly span_ℚ J, since it consists of finite rational combinations of elements of J and contains them all.

Define T=ℚ⊗_R M_R. The inclusion R⊂ℚ gives a commutative R-algebra structure on ℚ. Apply M002 to the R-basis m: the n vectors 1⊗m_i form a ℚ-basis of T. M010 applies to the nontrivial commutative ring ℚ. M003 with this basis gives dim_ℚ T=n, since |I|=n by N001.

Define Θ:T→U^I by Θ(q₀⊗Σ c_i e_i)=(q₀⊗c_i)_i, and define Ψ in the reverse direction by summing the maps q₀⊗c↦q₀⊗(c e_i) on coordinates. The coordinate maps in F001 are R-linear, so these balanced maps extend to ℚ-linear maps of the indicated tensor products. The composites ΘΨ and ΨΘ are identities: on an elementary tensor in a single coordinate the first is that same coordinate tensor, and on q₀⊗z the second is q₀⊗Σ c_i e_i=q₀⊗z. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove the identities everywhere. Therefore Θ is a linear equivalence. Set r_J=dim_ℚ U. By F002, U is finitely generated over ℚ, and M009 says it is free. With M010 supplying the strong rank condition for ℚ, apply M004 to the finite constant family U indexed by I; it gives dim_ℚ(U^I)=Σ_(i∈I)r_J=n r_J. Apply M005 to Θ and combine with F003 to obtain n=n r_J. Since n>0 by N001, integer arithmetic yields r_J=1.

Choose a nonzero a∈J from F001. Then 1⊗a is nonzero in U, since μ(1⊗a)=a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent: multiplying a putative scalar relation by μ gives that scalar times a zero in ℂ. Apply M001 over ℚ to this singleton and U, whose finite dimension is one by F002 and F004. It spans U. Consequently every 1⊗g_j is q_j(1⊗a) for some rational q_j; apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. As every g_j≠0, each q_j≠0. This proves existence of the full finite rational family needed next.

Choose q from F005, and fix 1≤j≤k. Write q_j=A/B with its nonzero integer numerator A and positive integer denominator B. By H001, p≥2, so p≠1. Apply M007 first to |A|≠0, then to B≠0, with ℓ=p. Choose d_N,u_N,d_D,u_D as in those applications, so |A|=p^d_N u_N, B=p^d_D u_D and neither u_N nor u_D is divisible by p. They are nonzero because A,B are. Hence q_j=p^(d_N−d_D)((A/|A|)u_N/u_D). Since A/|A| is either 1 or −1, the rational (A/|A|)u_N/u_D and its inverse belong to R by the defining denominator condition, so this factor is a unit. This proves, for every j in the finite list, the claimed decomposition into an integral power of p and a unit of R, and therefore the existence of simultaneous finite families in F006.

Choose ν_j,u_j from F006 and let ν be the minimum of the finite nonempty integer list ν_1,...,ν_k; choose j₀ attaining it. Such a minimum exists by repeatedly taking the smaller of two integers. Put b=p^ν a. This is nonzero, since p≠0 and a≠0. For each j, g_j=p^(ν_j−ν)u_j b lies in Rb because ν_j−ν≥0. Conversely g_(j₀)=u_(j₀)b, so b=u_(j₀)^(-1)g_(j₀) belongs to J. Thus the R-module generated by the g_j is exactly Rb, and J=Rb. Under F001, every vector of M_R is a sum Σ r_i b e_i, while any relation Σ r_i b e_i=0 has all r_i b=0 by the complex independence of e in N001, and hence all r_i=0. Thus (b e_i) is an R-basis. The same spanning and independence argument works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001, F002 and F004 this proves the exported conclusion.

R004.text: By H001, an integer maps to zero in K exactly when divisible by p. Thus for arbitrary integers A₀,B₀ with B₀≠0 and p∤B₀, the fraction A₀/B₀∈R has a nonzero denominator image in K; and φ(A₀/B₀)=(A₀·1_K)(B₀·1_K)^(-1) is defined. Equality of fractions follows by cross multiplication, so the formula is well-defined and preserves addition, multiplication and 1. The same formula in F_p gives ψ:R→F_p. It is onto, since every integer residue occurs, and its kernel is pR: ψ(A₀/B₀)=0 is equivalent to p∣A₀, hence A₀/B₀=p((A₀/p)/B₀). Conversely multiples of p have zero image. The induced map R/pR→F_p is therefore a bijective ring map. Both constructions agree with the usual inclusion F_p→K. Every unit of R has nonzero image in K, since its image has a multiplicative inverse. In particular N002 shows that r! for 0≤r≤λ and binom(λ,j), j∈I, have nonzero images in K.

Define Γ and Γ' by Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c and Γ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗φ(r)c. The defining ℤ-balancing relations in R⊗_ℤ M and in M⊗_ℤ K, and the R-balancing relation in M_R⊗_R K, show that these formulas extend to K-linear maps. They are inverse: Γ'Γ(m⊗c)=m⊗c, and ΓΓ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗φ(r)c=(r⊗m)⊗c. These tensors generate, so the composites are identities. Next define Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c and Δ'([z]⊗c)=z⊗c. Because p acts as zero on K, changing the lift z by pz' changes the second formula by pz'⊗c=z'⊗pc=0. Using F001, scalar balancing in F_p=R/pR gives the remaining balancing condition; thus both maps are well-defined and K-linear. Their composites are identities on pure tensors. This proves the two scalar-extension isomorphisms with exactly the formulas in the exported conclusion. An operator preserving M extends on all these tensors by applying it to the lattice factor; the displayed formulas commute with that operation. For Δ this also holds for any R-linear operator of M_R, since it preserves pM_R.

Choose b≠0 with J=Rb from N003. That input proves that (b e_i)_(i∈I), regarded in M_R via the injective map ι_M of N002, is an R-basis. Apply M002 with R₀=R, S₀=K and this basis, using φ from F001. It yields the K-basis (1⊗b e_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The tensor flip z⊗c↦c⊗z is K-linear, well-defined by balancing, and inverse to the reverse flip. Therefore (b e_i⊗1) is a basis of M_R⊗_R K. Transporting it by Γ^(-1) gives the K-basis β_i defined above: inverse linear maps carry spanning families to spanning families and relations to the same relations. Apply M010 to the nontrivial commutative field K, then M003 to β to obtain dim_K V_K=|I|=n>0 using N001.

Put a=ρ_K(x⊗1), d=ρ_K(y⊗1), t=ρ_K(h⊗1). By N001, complex linearity gives x(b e_i)=b x e_i, y(b e_i)=b y e_i, and h(b e_i)=b h e_i. N002 guarantees all these lattice operations are defined, and F002 transports their tensors. Thus aβ_0=0; aβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_(i−1) for i≥1; dβ_i=(i+1)β_(i+1) for i<λ, dβ_λ=0; tβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The coefficients are the images of the same integers in K. The identical reasoning using N001 for X(r),Y(r) gives their integral divided-power matrices on this basis for all r≥0, including the stated zero cases. Likewise each E_ij preserves M_R by N002 and acts there by E_ij(b e_k)=b e_i if k=j and equals zero otherwise, so its scalar extension, transported by Γ^(-1), is the coordinate matrix unit of β.

Fix 0≤r≤λ. As operators on M, the characteristic-zero definitions give r!X(r)=x^r and r!Y(r)=y^r; N002 gives their preservation of M. Tensoring these equalities gives the same equalities of induced operators on V_K. By F001, r!≠0 in K, so the induced divided powers equal (r!)^(-1)a^r and (r!)^(-1)d^r. The equality E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)Y(λ)X(λ)Y(λ−j) in N002 is an equality of R-linear operators on M_R. Extending scalars and transporting by Γ^(-1) preserves sums and compositions: this follows directly by evaluating on each pure tensor z⊗c. Substitute the divided-power equalities, whose indices λ−i, λ, λ−j all lie between 0 and λ. The result is T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)((λ−i)!)^(-1)a^(λ−i) (λ!)^(-1)d^λ (λ!)^(-1)a^λ ((λ−j)!)^(-1)d^(λ−j), with rightmost factor applied first. Every scalar inverse exists by F001. F004 gives T_ij β_k=β_i if k=j and zero otherwise. Along with F001–F004 this proves every assertion of the exported conclusion, including the two natural tensor identifications and positive dimension.

R005.text: N002 proves x,y,h preserve M and their integer span is a Lie algebra, which supplies the construction guard for ρ_K. Choose β from N004; set a,d,T as declared. N004 states that every scalar inverse in the polynomial T exists and T_ijβ_k equals β_i when k=j and zero otherwise. Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1). Thus a and d preserve W. Repeated composition shows by finite induction that every nonnegative power of either preserves W; the identity also preserves W. Composing these powers and multiplying by K-scalars preserves W by the subspace axioms. Every polynomial T_ij in N004 therefore preserves W.

First temporarily assume L3: W={0}. Then the disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately; discharge L3, giving F002. For the other branch temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. By this inequality and the subspace zero axiom, some nonzero vector lies in W. Expanding it in the basis β gives coefficients in K. If all coefficients were zero the vector would be zero, so at least one coefficient is nonzero. This establishes the simultaneous witnesses in F003 before choosing them.

Under L2 choose w,c,j from F003. For any i∈I, F001 and K-linearity give T_ij w=Σ_(k∈I)c_k T_ijβ_k=c_jβ_i∈W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives β_i∈W. As i was arbitrary, every vector in the basis β lies in W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 to obtain F004.

The alternatives W={0} and W≠{0} exhaust all cases. F002 and F004 therefore yield W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W to obtain the required assertion for every invariant K-subspace. N001 gives n=λ+1>0 and N004 gives a K-basis of V_K of that cardinality, so V_K is nonzero. The three generators span L_K, so their invariant subspaces are exactly L_K-submodules by K-linearity of ρ_K. H001 includes λ=0 and p=2: at λ=0 all powers and factorials used in T are zeroth powers and 1; if p=2 then λ is 0 or 1, and all preceding invertibilities still hold. No distinctness of h-eigenvalues in K was used; distinctness was used only over ℂ in N001. K was used solely as a field of characteristic p, so it need not be algebraically closed. This proves the full exported target.
